On this page

Architecture Overview ​

Principles ​

  1. Products compose applications; applications compose modules. A product is the solution people use. An application is a deployable program for one target role. Modules provide reusable business capabilities inside it.
  2. Write only business logic. Routes, permissions, sidebar, SDUI schemas, manifests and configuration files are generated at compile time.
  3. No manual registry, no magic strings. Everything is declared with attributes (#[panel], #[resource], #[permissions], #[gate], ...) and collected by the compile-time scanner.
  4. Context is implicit. The scanner knows the current module, so you write Refund, not sales.refund. The full path is still accepted.
  5. Secure by default. A write handler without #[gate] does not compile.
  6. One file, one responsibility. One resource per file. No catch-all mod.rs or admin.rs.
  7. One entry point. The Feluqa developer kit (SDK) provides a consistent Rust interface for application capabilities such as user interfaces, panels, authentication, and resources.
  8. Server is the source of truth. Hiding something in the client is never protection.

The pieces and where they run ​

PieceRoleWhen it mattersWhere it runs
Feluqa SDKThe library you build with: attributes, the compile-time scanner, the single feluqa namespace.While you write and compileDeveloper machine, linked into the Application
Feluqa CLICreates, validates, builds, installs and operates projects.Development and operationsDeveloper machine and servers
Feluqa PlatformAuthentication, access control, audit, configuration, System panel.RuntimeServer
ApplicationA target-specific program composed of one or more modules.RuntimeServer, workstation, mobile, or another target

Most people work with these four parts through the application and its tools.

From modules to application artifacts ​

A Product can provide several Applications for different target roles. Each Application composes the modules it needs; each target build produces an artifact for that Application and target profile.

The SDUI schema sent to the client is already filtered server-side: an entry the user may not see is never serialized.

What is generated and never edited ​

Generated into target/feluqa/, never edited and never committed:

  • module manifests and the route table;
  • the permission table (consumed by the System panel);
  • configuration schemas and .env.example;
  • reference documentation.

feluqa.toml (application) and module.toml (module) are build contexts. The current CLI creates the application manifest with feluqa new; module generation remains a separate capability.

Target profiles ​

ProfileTypical useStorageStatus
serverHosted backend, multi-user web appPostgreSQL, or SQLite for small single-server installsPartial
workstationStandalone local app on a desktopSQLite in the user data directoryTarget
embedded (no_std)Telemetry, sensor ingestionMinimal or noneExploring

Shared Modules are intended to work across separate Applications built for different target profiles. Server and workstation composition, connectivity, synchronization, and offline behavior remain product goals whose design is still being worked out.

Interaction surfaces and desktop hosts ​

An application's target profile and its interaction surface are separate choices. workstation describes where and how the application runtime is deployed; console, graphical, or mixed describes how a person interacts with it. A console application is therefore not limited to a shell window on the developer's operating system.

Feluqa may provide a workstation host that presents a console application in a terminal-style desktop window. A separate product experience could combine a graphical desktop interface with an integrated terminal for console commands. These experiences need a desktop host that connects the window to the Feluqa console runtime; a Rust binary or a workstation profile alone does not provide that host. Neither desktop terminal experience is currently implemented. Host-shell selection and its build configuration remain product and architecture work.

Platform capabilities ​

ComponentPurpose
Feluqa CLICreates, validates, builds, installs, and operates projects, modules, and applications.
ModulesSelf-contained units of business functionality with their own version, permissions, and features.
Target profilesSelect dependencies and capabilities for server, workstation, and constrained no_std builds.
Feluqa SDKProvides attributes, panels, resources, and the compile-time scanner through a single feluqa entry point.
Feluqa PlatformThe planned server-side runtime and control plane, including a System panel for authentication, schema management, and access control.
AuthorizationDefines privileges, roles, permissions, and policies. Runtime authorization remains necessary even when compile-time checks are available.
StorageUses embedded SQLite as the proposed local default, with other strategies depending on deployment needs.

Design targets ​

These figures and capabilities are design targets, not measured guarantees; they have not yet been revalidated.

AreaTargetWhy it matters
LanguageNative RustMemory safety and control over runtime costs.
Hot-path latencySub-millisecond p50A target for selected operations, not an end-to-end or real-time guarantee.
Local persistenceSQLite by defaultReduces setup requirements for standalone deployments.
Security boundariesSeparate platform, application, and user scopesMakes ownership and access rules explicit.
Access controlPrivileges, roles, permissions, and policiesCombines compile-time validation where possible with runtime authorization.
